name: Pipeline
notes: World-famous barreling wave with powerful, hollow tubes; best suited to experienced surfers

name: Teahupo'o
notes: Heavy, shallow reef break with exceptionally thick barrels; only for advanced surfers

name: Jeffreys Bay
notes: Long, fast right-hand point break with multiple sections; excellent on a good swell

name: Uluwatu
notes: Iconic reef break with several sections and consistent waves; crowded but offers options for experienced surfers

name: Cloudbreak
notes: Powerful left-hand reef break with long barrels; can become extremely heavy on larger swells

name: Bells Beach
notes: Iconic long-running right-hand point break with powerful walls; best with solid southwest swell

name: Mundaka
notes: World-famous left-hand barrel over a river mouth; highly dependent on swell, tide, and sandbar conditions

name: Supertubos
notes: Fast, hollow beach break famous for powerful barrels; shifting peaks and strong currents

name: Puerto Escondido
notes: Powerful beach break with heavy barrels; can be extremely dangerous when large but offers excellent waves at manageable size

name: Mavericks
notes: Famous big-wave break with enormous, cold-water waves; strictly for highly experienced big-wave surfers

name: Matunuck
notes: Great wave but crowded, long walk-out over cobblestone boulders at lower tides
